orgTagsFilter.description:
Filter expression for targeting organizations by tags for policy application.

### Operators
| Operator | Description | Example |
| -------- | ----------- | ------- |
| co | Contains | tags co 'service:level' |
| eq | Equal | tags eq 'region:us-east' |
| ne | Not Equal | tags ne 'service:level:basic' |

### Usage Notes
* Operators are case-sensitive (lowercase only)
* Combine filters with 'and'/'or'
* Group with parentheses for precedence

### Examples
| Expression | Matches |
| ---------- | ------- |
| tags eq 'service:level:basic' | Organizations with exact tag |
| tags co 'service:level' | Organizations with tags containing substring |
| (tags eq 'region:us-east' or tags eq 'region:us-west') | Organizations in either region |
| (tags eq 'service:level:premium' and tags co 'region:us') | Premium organizations in US regions |

Filter expression for targeting organizations by tags for policy application.

### Operators
| Operator | Description | Example |
| -------- | ----------- | ------- |

* Group with parentheses for precedence

| ---------- | ------- |

| (tags eq 'region:us-east' or tags eq 'region:us-west') | Organizations in either region |
| (tags eq 'service:level:premium' and tags co 'region:us') | Premium organizations in US regions |

info.description:
[Flexera's Automation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/AutomationGS.htm) uses Policies to automate governance across your multi-cloud environment to increase agility and efficiency while managing risk for your organization.

The API is available at the following endpoints, dependent upon the user/tenant zone:
| Zone        | Base URL    |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| NAM         | https://api.flexera.com/ |
| EU          | https://api.flexera.eu/ |
| APAC        | https://api.flexera.au/ |

To create an [Applied Policy](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/ApplyPolicies.htm) in Flexera's Automation, you must either create a policy template or choose from one of Flexera's existing templates provided through the published templates API. These templates are also available on the Catalog page in the Automation section of the UI. More information about our existing policy templates are publicly available [on Github](https://github.com/flexera-public/policy_templates) including what must be provided to apply them. After a template is applied, an Applied Policy will run on cadence based on its schedule until it is terminated. On runs where it discovers information which meets its specified criteria, an incident will be generated to alert users of items violating the policy.

Index returns a list of published templates which can be filtered by the catalogSource parameter. 
The default setting only includes templates made available to all MSP child orgs.
Using different catalogSource value enables users to preview what templates will be available to their child orgs with other "policy-catalog-reference-org" settings.
This setting can be changed at the [Customization Value](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Customization%20Value) endpoint.

parameters.description:
Optional filter to retrieve published templates based on specific criteria.
### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter                    | Type   | Example                                   | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------    | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| name                      | string | name in ['policy123', 'policy124']        | Returns published templates named either 'policy123' or 'policy124'                   |
| shortDescription          | string | shortDescription co 'disks'               | Returns published templates with a shortDescription containing 'disks'                |
| longDescription           | string | longDescription co 'cloud'                | Returns published templates with a longDescription containing 'cloud'                 |
| docLink                   | string | docLink co 'README'                       | Returns published templates with a docLink containing 'README'                        |
| category                  | string | category in ['compliance', 'cost']        | Returns published templates with 'compliance' or 'cost' as category                   |
| createdBy.email           | string | createdBy.email eq 'foouser@email.com'    | Returns published templates created by user with email equal to 'foouser@email.com'   |
| createdAt                 | time   | createdAt gt '2022-05-20T00:00:00Z'       | Returns published templates created after 2022-05-20                                  |

tags.description:
**In Preview: not currently supported in production.**
	
An action status is the status of an action after it is executed by an [escalation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Escalations.htm) or by a [resolution](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Resolutions.htm) raised by an [incident](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/AboutPolicies.htm#aboutpolicies_2371672742_1084494) of an [applied policy template](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Applied%20Policy).

Actions can be sending emails, requesting manual approvals, or running cloud workflows. The possible statuses for actions are:

- Queued: The initial status of an action.
- Aborted: When the incident of the action was deleted.
- Pending: When awaiting the user's approval.
- Running: When the action is in progress.
- Completed: When all the tasks for an action are completed.
- Failed: When the action had an error.
- Denied: When the user denies the action.

**Escalations** are sequences of actions that are triggered when a policy validation fails, indicating a compliance or configuration issue.

**Resolutions** are sequences of actions that are executed when a previously failed policy condition is corrected, indicating that compliance has been restored.
tags.name: Action Status

tags.description: A policy aggregate represents a grouping of policies for a particular organization providing an overview and aggregation of those policies. It provides insights and statistics about the policies and their compliance within the organization.

tags.description: A policy manager represents a mechanism for orchestrating policy execution across multiple organizations in MSP (Managed Service Provider) environments. It allows filtering target organizations using tags and provides centralized control over policy deployment, scheduling, and management. Policy managers work exclusively with published templates at the organization level and maintain consistent governance across child organizations.
tags.name: Policy Manager

tags.description:
A published template is a policy template published from a project to an organization. All organizations have access to a catalog of
Published Templates provided by Flexera in the [Flexera Automation Catalog](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/PoliciesList.htm). 
These templates can be viewed in the [Flexera-Public Github Repository](https://github.com/flexera-public/policy_templates).

Users can also create their own custom policy templates and publish them. Catalog and custom published templates can be distinguished by the 'builtIn' attribute.
This will only be true for published templates from the Flexera Automation Catalog.
tags.name: Published Template

tags.description:
A Policy Template is a program written in the [Policy Template Language](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/PTL.htm).
These templates are used to automate compliance standards, cost management, operational tasks, security, and other repeatable tasks.
They are run by 'being applied' and creating an Applied Policy.
More information on applying a template can be found in the [Applied Policies API](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Applied%20Policy).

Example templates can be viewed in the [Flexera-Public Github Repository](https://github.com/flexera-public/policy_templates).
A selection of these templates are available to all users in the Automation Catalog or by querying the [Published Templates API](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Published%20Template).

Users can create their own policy templates or modify exiting templates and upload them to a project in their Org.
Documentation for building these templates can be found at [Policy Template Language Documentation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/PTL.htm).
Once a template is ready for testing, it can be [uploaded to Flexera One](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/CreateCustomPolicy.htm#automationrefinfo_2830531361_1243084).

Policy templates **must have unique names** in the project they are uploaded in.
The name of a policy template is inside the [metadata section](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/Metadata.htm).

Policy Templates can be applied ONLY in the project where they were uploaded. When a template is published in the Automation Catalog, other projects in the organization can also apply the policy.
tags.name: Policy Template

tags.description:
Customization Type provides organizations with a list of all available customization options for the Automation capability. These are read-only
and changes to their values can be made by interacting with the [Customization Value](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Customization%20Value) API.
For example, a user could look up the "policy-published-by-email" customization type here and see that it is used to describe the authors of Catalog Templates
in the Automation Catalog and used by customers as a helpline to send questions about templates. If the user then wanted to have this replaced by a different
support email, they could use the Customization Value endpoint to do so.
tags.name: Customization Type

tags.description:
Customization Value stores and retrieves custom values for [Customization Types](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/policy/v1#/Customization%20Type).
Adding a customization value will replace the default value for your Organization and all of your [MSP Child Orgs](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/api/iam/v1#/MSP%20Customer). Removing it will do the same. All changes
will go into effect immediately. Some changes, such as those to the emails, will not affect existing assets, but will be applied to all items created
after the fact. For example, if you change your email header logo, it will not change the logo on emails already sent, but emails sent after the change
will have the updated logo.
tags.name: Customization Value

tags.description: An applied policy represents policy template code that is evaluated on a fixed schedule that is configured by the user applying the policy. The schedule can range from 15 minutes to monthly depending on the needs and requirements of the policy and will run on that schedule until terminated by a user.
tags.name: Applied Policy

tags.description:
**In Preview: not currently supported in production.**

An Archived Incident is a partial copy of an eligible inactive [incident](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/AboutPolicies.htm#aboutpolicies_2371672742_1084494) which has been deleted during the archiving process.

Inactive incidents are incidents which either have had their associated applied policy terminated or incidents which have been resolved. Inactive incidents become eligible to be archived after 30 days of entering that terminated or resolved state. Resolved incidents which currently have one or more resolutions running on them will not be archived until all resolutions have finished running.

During the archiving process all incident fields except the data and detail will be saved to the archived incident and then the incident will be deleted. The archived incident will remain accessible for one year before it is permanently deleted as well.
tags.name: Archived Incident

tags.description:
The Custom Catalog service allows MSP parent organizations to manage custom catalog settings for published templates.
These settings include visibility controls and other configurations that define how child organizations access and use these templates.
This helps MSP parents enforce governance and standardization across their managed child organizations.
This API is not available to non-MSP customers.
tags.name: CustomCatalog
